analysis.title: GS MORNING: Equities Update, Hatzius on Downside Risks to Growth, SGD/INR Carry Idea, NatGas Update and GS FX Webcast Today (24 Nov 2026)
key_insights: GS retains Buy on Nvidia with a 12-month PT of $220 (22x P/E on normalized EPS of $10.00). Jensen Huang's reinstatement as CEO is expected to support a multiple re-rate, though reported investigations still weigh.

Privorotsky describes a massive short squeeze after shorts were added into end of last week and asks whether the 'Trump put' is back. Huang's return reduces doubt over Nvidia's willingness to keep underwriting the AI buildout.
Asia AI trade ripped: CoreWeave +22%, Taiwan +9%, TSMC and Foxconn limit up, Kospi +6.5% led by Samsung and SK Hynix, Nikkei +4%. China lagged with CSI 300 +0.14% and Hang Seng -0.73% in early trade.

Chip export watch: the administration tightened rules on remote access to advanced chips last week. Key tells are whether Commerce grants licenses for Chinese customers via offshore data centers and whether Congress builds veto-proof support for tougher restrictions. Huang testifies Dec 1.

Hatzius lists three downside risks to the base case of steady global growth in 2027: renewed Iran escalation hitting real income, bond turbulence in the Euro Area and France ahead of the presidential election (deficit ~5.5% of GDP), and a sharper AI investment slowdown or labour market hit.

SGD/INR carry idea: buy 6m dual digital, USDSGD above ATM and USDINR below 2% ITM, costing 14.4% USD, with max loss limited to premium paid. Entry supported by AI sentiment recovery, month-end importer hedging and potential RBI smoothing.

India equity inflows reached nearly US$12bn in November, and long-only funds were ~175bp underweight India at end-September. A return to neutral implies roughly US$24bn of inflows, which is supportive for INR unless the RBI absorbs flows.

India underlying BOP is about -US$4bn/month before portfolio flows. RBI letting oil companies source USD directly could remove ~US$10bn/month of USD demand. GS expects meaningful RBI dollar buying around 92 once the ~US$13bn NDF short is covered.

Europe gas: colder forecasts drove TTF to EUR 90/MWh (+6% WoW). A cold shock without offsets would leave NW Europe storage only 14% full at end-winter vs the 20% base case, the lowest since the 2018 record-low 9%.

If the cold holds, GS estimates TTF would need to reach EUR 106/MWh to attract enough LNG, vs the EUR 65/MWh 1Q27 base case under average weather. Persian Gulf LNG exports fell from over 60% of pre-war levels in early Nov to 25% last week, keeping supply risk alive.
GS FX webcast on the 2027 FX Outlook is scheduled for 2pm London on 24 Nov.
